q: Rokhlin's cocycle theorem: for an ergodic measure-preserving transformation T and a measurable function φ: X → ℝ (a cocycle), the Birkhoff sums Sₙφ(x) = Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} φ(T^k x) are centered if ∫φ dμ = 0. The CLT (central limit theorem) for Birkhoff sums holds (with √n normalization) when:
opts: φ satisfies a mixing condition and is sufficiently regular (e.g., Hölder for hyperbolic systems via the spectral gap of the transfer operator)
exp: CLT for Birkhoff sums: (1/√n) Sₙφ → N(0,σ²) (in distribution) when the system is mixing and φ is regular enough (Hölder). The proof uses the spectral gap of the Ruelle-Perron-Frobenius operator. For hyperbolic systems, this gives statistical laws for chaotic trajectories.
